chapters.title: Number System
theory: Natural, whole, integer, rational, irrational numbers. Prime = exactly 2 factors; 1 prime nahi hai.
Divisibility: 3/9 = digit sum; 4 = last 2 digits; 8 = last 3; 11 = alternate digit sum ka difference 0 ya 11 ka multiple.
N = a^p x b^q ho to factors = (p+1)(q+1).
short_tricks: Unit digit: power ko 4 se divide karo; remainder 0 ho to power 4 lo.
1 se n tak sum = n(n+1)/2.

chapters.title: HCF and LCM
theory: HCF = sabse bada common divisor. LCM = sabse chhota common multiple.
Do numbers ke liye: HCF x LCM = product.
Fractions: HCF = HCF(num)/LCM(den); LCM = LCM(num)/HCF(den).
short_tricks: HCF ke liye numbers ka difference check karo.
'Same remainder k' wale sawal: LCM + k.

chapters.title: Percentage
theory: a% increase ke baad b% change: net = a + b + ab/100 (decrease negative).
short_tricks: x% of y = y% of x.

chapters.title: Simple Interest
theory: SI = P x R x T / 100. Amount = P + SI.
short_tricks: SI har saal same rehta hai.

chapters.title: Compound Interest
theory: Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T. CI = Amount - P.
Half-yearly: rate aadha, periods double.
short_tricks: 2 saal ka CI - SI = P(R/100)^2.
3 saal: P x r^2 x (3+r), r = R/100.

chapters.title: Installments
theory: CI: borrowed sum = har instalment ki present value ka sum.
SI (due debt): A = Tx + x R T(T-1)/200.
short_tricks: Present value = x/(1+r)^t.

chapters.title: Profit, Loss and Discount
theory: Profit = SP - CP. Profit% CP par nikalta hai.
Discount Marked Price (MP) par hota hai. SP = MP(100-d)/100.
short_tricks: Successive discount a, b: a + b - ab/100.

chapters.title: Time and Work
theory: A kaam d din me kare to 1 din ka kaam 1/d.
M1 D1 H1 / W1 = M2 D2 H2 / W2.
short_tricks: LCM method: total work = LCM of days, phir efficiency nikalo.

short_tricks: Time and Work jaisa hi LCM method lagao.

chapters.title: Ratio, Proportion and Partnership
theory: a:b = c:d ho to ad = bc.
Partnership: profit ratio = investment x time.
short_tricks: Ratio parts ka sum nikalo, phir 1 part ki value.

chapters.title: Problems on Ages

Do logon ka age difference hamesha constant rehta hai.

chapters.title: Mixtures and Alligation

chapters.title: Averages
theory: Average = Sum / Count. Sum = Average x Count.

chapters.title: Data Interpretation and Set Theory

chapters.title: Permutation and Combination

Order matter kare to P, warna C.

chapters.title: Probability
theory: P(E) = favourable / total. 0 se 1 ke beech.
P(not E) = 1 - P(E).
short_tricks: 'At least one' = 1 - P(none).
Do dice: 36 outcomes. Cards: 52, 4 suits, 12 face cards.

km/h se m/s: x 5/18.

chapters.title: Boats and Streams

chapters.title: Mensuration

chapters.title: Statistics

Variance = (x - mean)^2 ka average. SD = root(variance).

chapters.title: Reading Comprehension
theory: Passage 1: Many students prepare for placements by solving a large number of questions. Volume helps them recognise common patterns, but it can also create a false sense of progress. A student who reads the solution immediately after getting stuck may feel that the idea is clear, yet fail to produce it alone a week later. A better method is to attempt the problem for a fixed time, study the solution, and then solve it again after a gap. Keeping a short record of mistakes also shows whether errors come from weak concepts, careless reading or poor time management.

Passage 2: A small software team began holding a ten-minute meeting each morning. At first, members used it to report everything they had done, and the meeting often ran for half an hour. The lead then asked each person to mention only the day's goal and any obstacle. Detailed discussions were moved to later, with only the relevant people attending. The meetings became shorter, and blocked tasks were noticed earlier. The team did not claim that meetings solved technical problems; they only made it easier to see where help was needed.
Q1-4 Passage 1 par, Q5-8 Passage 2 par.
short_tricks: Pehle question padho, phir passage me line dhoondo.

chapters.title: Cloze Test
theory: Passage: Learning to code takes (1) practice. Beginners often (2) errors, but each error offers a clue. Instead of (3) the whole program, a good programmer tests small parts (4). This makes it easier to (5) the source of a bug. Over time, patience becomes as (6) as knowledge of syntax. Writing clear names also helps others (7) the code. Finally, reviewing old programs shows how far one has (8).
short_tricks: Blank ke aage-peeche ke words se part of speech pehchano.

since = starting point, for = duration. Each/every ke saath singular verb.

drills.title: Email Writing 2: Delay Update
drills.prompt: Client ko batao ki report 1 din late hogi. Reason: data late mila. Mention: nayi date, abhi tak ka progress, apology.
drills.sample_input: 540 seconds (9 minutes) | Subject + Greeting + Purpose + Details + Closing
drills.hint: Cover every mentioned point concisely in formal business English with a clear Subject, Greeting, and Sign-off.
drills.solution_text:
Subject: Revised Delivery Date for the Monthly Report
Dear Ms. Rao,
I am writing to inform you that the monthly report will be delayed by one day
because we received the required data late. The analysis framework and the first
draft are ready. We will share the complete report by Tuesday, 15 December.
I apologise for the inconvenience and appreciate your understanding.
Regards,
Aman

drills.title: Email Writing 3: Training Request
drills.prompt: Manager se ek online C++ training join karne ki permission maango. Mention: fayda, timing, kaam par asar nahi.
drills.sample_input: 540 seconds (9 minutes) | Subject + Greeting + Purpose + Details + Closing
drills.hint: Cover every mentioned point concisely in formal business English with a clear Subject, Greeting, and Sign-off.
drills.solution_text:
Subject: Request to Attend C++ Training
Dear Mr. Khan,
I would like your permission to attend an online C++ training programme. It will
help me write more efficient and maintainable code for our projects. The sessions
are on Saturday mornings, so they will not affect my regular work.
Please let me know if I may enrol.
Regards,
Aman

drills.title: P1. Reverse a Number
drills.prompt: Non-negative integer N ke digits reverse karo.
drills.hint: % 10 se digit nikalo. O(digits).

drills.title: P2. Palindrome String
drills.prompt: String (bina space) palindrome hai to YES, warna NO.
drills.hint: Reverse karke compare. O(n).

drills.title: P3. Prime Check
drills.prompt: N prime hai ya nahi (YES/NO).
drills.hint: Sirf root(N) tak check karo.

drills.title: P4. Fibonacci Term
drills.hint: Do variables rakho. long long use karo.

drills.title: P5. GCD and LCM
drills.prompt: Do positive integers (10^9 tak) ka GCD aur LCM.
drills.hint: Euclid algorithm. LCM me pehle divide karo.

drills.title: P6. Armstrong Number
drills.prompt: N Armstrong hai? (digits ki power digit-count ka sum = N)
drills.hint: Digits ko string se lo, integer power banao.

drills.title: P7. Count Vowels
drills.prompt: Ek word me vowels gino.
drills.hint: string::find use karo.

drills.title: P8. Second Largest
drills.prompt: Input: N, phir N integers. Second largest distinct value, na ho to -1. Values non-negative.
drills.hint: set sorted aur unique rakhta hai. O(n log n).

drills.title: P9. Move Zeros
drills.prompt: Input: N, phir N integers. Zeros end me le jao, baaki order same.
drills.hint: Two pointer. O(n).

drills.title: P10. Rotate Array Right
drills.prompt: Input: N, K, phir N integers. Array ko right me K baar rotate karo.
drills.hint: K %= N, phir rotate.

drills.title: P11. Missing Number
drills.prompt: Input: N, phir 1..N me se N-1 distinct numbers. Missing batao.
drills.hint: Expected sum - actual sum.

drills.title: P12. Anagram Check
drills.prompt: Do lowercase words anagram hain? YES/NO.
drills.hint: Dono sort karke compare.

drills.title: P13. First Non-Repeating Character
drills.prompt: Lowercase word ka pehla non-repeating character, na ho to -1.
drills.hint: Pehle frequency, phir dobara traverse.

drills.title: P14. Two Sum
drills.prompt: Input: N, T, phir N integers. Do alag index (0-based) jinka sum T ho; na ho to -1.
drills.hint: unordered_map me pehle dekhe values. Average O(n).

drills.title: P15. Matrix Diagonal Sum
drills.prompt: Input: N, phir N x N matrix. Dono diagonals ka sum (center ek baar).
drills.hint: j==i ya j==n-1-i.

drills.title: P16. Maximum Subarray
drills.prompt: Input: N, phir N integers. N >= 1. Contiguous subarray ka maximum sum.
drills.hint: Kadane. O(n).

drills.title: P17. Longest Unique Substring
drills.prompt: Bina space string ki longest substring jisme repeat na ho; length batao.
drills.hint: Sliding window. O(n).

drills.title: P18. Subarrays With Sum K
drills.prompt: Input: N, K, phir N integers. Sum K wale subarrays gino.
drills.hint: Prefix sum + map. O(n log n).

drills.title: P19. Balanced Brackets
drills.prompt: Sirf ()[]{} wali string balanced hai? YES/NO.
drills.hint: Stack. O(n).

drills.title: P20. Binary Search First Position
drills.prompt: Input: N, T, phir sorted N integers. T ka pehla index (0-based), na ho to -1.
drills.hint: lower_bound. Search O(log n).

drills.title: P21. Merge Intervals
drills.prompt: Input: N, phir N pairs L R (L <= R). Overlap/touch karne wale merge karke print karo.
drills.hint: Start se sort karo. O(n log n).

drills.title: P22. Climbing Stairs
drills.prompt: Ek baar me 1 ya 2 step. N steps (1..90) chadne ke ways.
drills.hint: DP: ways[n] = ways[n-1] + ways[n-2].

drills.title: P23. Minimum Coins
drills.prompt: Input: N, S, phir N positive coin values (unlimited). S (0..100000) banane ke minimum coins, na bane to -1.
drills.hint: DP. O(N x S).
